summary: This article explains why lakes can shrink or vanish, from seasonal desert lakes and a lake that drains through a hole to the Aral Sea, and how a damaged lake can recover.
introduce: Draw a simple cause → effect arrow on the board and ask students for an everyday example, such as “I did not sleep, so I felt tired.” Tell them that while reading “Lakes That Disappear” they will find at least two cause-and-effect links.

keyTerms.def: the change of a liquid, such as water, into a gas
bringing water to fields through pipes or channels so crops can grow
happening or existing only at certain times of the year

challengeTerms.def: to change the direction or use of something
a result or effect of an action, often an important one
able to continue for a long time without harming the environment

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that people are the main reason that lakes disappear? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain two different reasons a lake can disappear.
struggling: Pre-teach evaporation, irrigation, and seasonal with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers match cause cards to effect cards from the article with a partner.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use divert, consequence, and sustainable in a short paragraph that explains one important cause-and-effect chain from the article.
